findings.def: Published “astrology market” figures conflict by orders of magnitude — from ~$153M (horoscope apps) to $25–30B (2033 projections). The credible anchor: IBISWorld's US Psychic Services industry at $2.3B, 5.5% CAGR, 103,340 businesses, no firm above 5% share.
findings.sub: Large, slow-growing, highly fragmented — ideal terrain for infrastructure, hostile terrain for hype.

findings.def: US “nones” have plateaued near 29%; belief in astrology is statistically unchanged over eight years (27% in 2024 vs 29% in 2017). The bet is formalizing and equipping an existing large market — not surfing a demand explosion.
findings.sub: Pew Religious Landscape Study 2023–24; Gallup 1990s–2000s corroborates.

findings.def: 43% of women under 50 affirm astrology; 54% of LGBT adults consult horoscopes yearly and 33% use tarot — three times the national rate. But only 6% of Americans engage weekly and 1% rely on it for major decisions.
findings.sub: Pew Research Center, May 21 2025 · n = 9,593 US adults.

findings.def: The Vatican has confirmed a Holy Year of Redemption in 2033 — the 2,000th anniversary of the Resurrection, with a global evangelization push. It will raise the cultural salience of meaning-seeking broadly; it is also explicitly Christian and doctrinally anti-divination.
findings.sub: Treat as an attention tailwind to ride obliquely — never to co-opt. This spillover thesis is inferential, not proven.

findings.def: EU AI Act Article 5 (in force Feb 2025), California SB 243 (Jan 2026, private right of action), New York §1700 (Nov 2025), FTC's Operation AI Comply — all tightening in exactly the areas our guardrails and attestation address.
findings.sub: The human-vs-AI distinction is becoming a legal requirement. Compliance moves from cost to moat.

findings.def: Stripe restricts psychic services; practitioners lose accounts over vocabulary. Apple's Guideline 4.3 rejects fortune-telling apps serially (Struck: ~10 times). This is precisely why B2B infrastructure that solves compliant payments and web-first distribution is valuable.
findings.sub: The biggest risk and the biggest value proposition are the same fact.

findings.def: Consumer apps fight for attention; APIs sell computation; horizontal creator platforms won't build vertical depth. Nobody owns practitioner-first, white-label, AI-plus-human-attestation infrastructure for Western spiritual practitioners.
findings.sub: Closest structural analog: SimplePractice for therapists — 225,000+ clinicians, inside a ~$4B deal.

findings.def: Post-ChatGPT: 36% of translators lost work, freelance writing demand fell ~30%, stock photography pivoted to selling training data. Generic interpretation is commoditizing — while relationship-, brand-, and provenance-based work retains value. CHANI's ~$14M all-human business is the proof point.
findings.sub: Verified-human positioning is directionally value-accretive and increasingly legally favored. Validate the premium empirically; don't assume it.

caveats.def: “Leading the niche by 2033” is achievable only if the niche is Western spiritual-practitioner infrastructure — not the astrology market at large — and only if payments get solved early, capital or profitability arrives by ~2028, and the B2B2C discipline holds.

CHANI's ~$14M is an Inc. estimate reported secondhand. Sanctuary's funding trackers disagree ($4.55–10.3M). The viral “68% of tarot readers lost 40%+ income” claim traces to a promotional source — we cite it nowhere as fact.

Suggestive historical coincidence (the 2000-millennium New Age boom) but no rigorous study isolates Christian-observance spillover into non-Christian spiritual markets. A plausible attention tailwind — never a demand guarantee.
App-market forecasts ($4B→$29.8B at ~25% CAGR) are vendor sales collateral. We anchor planning on IBISWorld's $2.3B primary series and flag everything else.

sources.def: May 21, 2025 survey (n=9,593); Religious Landscape Study 2023–24. Engagement, demographics, and the plateau of the “nones.”
US Psychic Services (NAICS OD4413): $2.3B revenue, 5.5% CAGR, 103,340 businesses, ~100,000 employed, ~$1.5B wages.
EU AI Act Article 5; California SB 243; New York GBL §1700; FTC Operation AI Comply actions (DoNotPay, Workado).
Funding and revenue via credible press: Co-Star ($15M Series A), AstroTalk (₹651 crore FY24, ~$30M raised), Nebula (~$50M ARR), CHANI (Inc. estimate), Sanctuary (trackers conflict).
Society of Authors survey (Jan 2024); Bloomberry Upwork analysis (~5M postings); Demirci et al. 2024; Oxford machine-translation employment study.
Stripe restricted-business list; Apple App Review Guideline 4.3; Meta Personal Attributes advertising policy.
